set.prevailing_wage_basis: County of Santa Clara Supportive Housing Development Program Guidelines, Version 7 (term sheet September 28, 2021; approved by the Board November 16, 2021, Item 22, BOS-2021-168), Wages section: the County requires State prevailing wages to be paid when County funds are used for construction unless a project can demonstrate that it is otherwise exempt, at not less than the general prevailing rate under Labor Code 1773 and 8 CCR 16000 et seq.; if federal funds are used for physical improvements, the higher of State prevailing wage and Davis-Bacon rates applies. The guidelines state they apply to all of the County's housing development funds. The September 15, 2026 Board report for North 40 Phase II (item 127502) confirms County loans are still made under these guidelines as amended November 16, 2021 and the SHDF NOFA underwriting terms. https://sccgov.iqm2.com/Citizens/FileOpen.aspx?Type=4&ID=220345 ; https://sccgov.iqm2.com/Citizens/Detail_LegiFile.aspx?ID=107780 ; https://sccgov.iqm2.com/Citizens/FileOpen.aspx?Type=30&ID=230631 Practical effect: true by default, but a project that shows a Labor Code 1720(c) exemption is not required to pay State prevailing wage.

set.prevailing_wage_basis: Supportive Housing Fund Program Guidelines (revised May 22, 2017, effective October 1, 2017) Sections 5.1 and 7.1: borrowers must comply with the County of Santa Clara Prevailing Wage Requirements; except for projects of $1,000 or less, vendors performing building construction, alteration, demolition or repair must pay all workers on County-funded projects prevailing wage under Labor Code 1770 through 1777.7. These are still the guidelines linked from the live Housing Trust program page as of November 10, 2026. The County's current rule is the Supportive Housing Development Program Guidelines Version 7 (approved November 16, 2021), Wages section: State prevailing wage when County funds are used for construction unless the project demonstrates an exemption. https://housingtrustsv.org/wp-content/uploads/2019/11/Supportive-Housing-Fund-Guidelines.pdf ; https://housingtrustsv.org/programs/developer-funding/supportive-housing-fund/ ; https://sccgov.iqm2.com/Citizens/FileOpen.aspx?Type=4&ID=220345
set.layering_notes: Revolving fund created by County MOU June 9, 2015 and amended April 11, 2017 to implement the 2016 Measure A bond pipeline. Repayment is due at the close of County or other public land financing, construction closing or permanent closing. Program guidelines on the site date from 2017; confirm current terms. Prevailing wage is required by the fund guidelines (County Prevailing Wage Requirements), so budget State prevailing wage from the first draw. Pair with the County Office of Supportive Housing Measure A and Affordable Housing Fund records and with Destination: Home's Supportive Housing and Innovation Fund.
set.audit_note: PW audit Nov 10, 2026: Housing Trust program page still links the 2017 guidelines; County Version 7 guidelines (2021) confirm the County rule. layering_notes corrected (it said unclear while the trigger is true).

reason: Live program page still links the 2017 guidelines requiring County prevailing wage, consistent with the current County guidelines.

set.prevailing_wage_basis: No stated rule for the County land program itself. The County Supportive Housing Development Program Guidelines Version 7 (approved November 16, 2021, still cited as operative in the September 15, 2026 North 40 Phase II Board report) require State prevailing wage when County funds are used for construction unless the project demonstrates an exemption, so County gap loans paired with these sites carry the requirement; the guidelines do not address land conveyances. A ground lease or sale below fair market value is public funds under Labor Code 1720(b)(3), and coverage then depends on 1720(c) exemptions and project facts. https://sccgov.iqm2.com/Citizens/FileOpen.aspx?Type=4&ID=220345 ; https://sccgov.iqm2.com/Citizens/FileOpen.aspx?Type=30&ID=230631
set.audit_note: PW audit Nov 10, 2026: unclear kept; basis now cites the County Version 7 guidelines instead of the 2017 Housing Trust guidelines.

reason: Current County guidelines tie prevailing wage to County construction funds, not land conveyances, so unclear stands.

set.prevailing_wage_basis: HUD Notice PIH 2011-45 (Parameters for Local, Non-Traditional Activities under the MTW Demonstration, issued August 15, 2011, in effect until superseded), Labor standards: Davis-Bacon requirements under Section 12 of the 1937 Act apply at all units acquired, renovated and/or built using MTW funds; no nine-unit floor applies to MTW-funded development. 42 U.S.C. 1437j(a) is the underlying statute. If HACSM also attaches PBVs, 24 CFR 983.153(c) separately applies Davis-Bacon to PBV development with nine or more contract units. https://www.hud.gov/sites/documents/pih2011-45.pdf ; https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/42/1437j ; https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-24/subtitle-B/chapter-IX/part-983
set.layering_notes: Unusual source: HUD lets this MTW agency lend its unspent voucher money as capital, and the County has pushed the ceiling to $65,000,000. It arrives inside an AHF award as a zero-interest residual receipts loan, which helps cash flow versus the County's 3% Measure K loan. MTW-funded acquisition, rehab or construction carries federal Davis-Bacon on all units under HUD Notice PIH 2011-45 (Section 12 of the 1937 Act), plus Section 3; state prevailing wage turns on the County loan and the Labor Code 1720(c) exemptions. Read from the FY 2027 MTW Annual Plan PDF (opened).
set.audit_note: PW audit Nov 10, 2026: true confirmed from HUD Notice PIH 2011-45 (MTW local non-traditional activities); prior basis implied a nine-unit threshold that does not apply to MTW-funded development.

reason: HUD PIH 2011-45 applies Davis-Bacon to all units acquired, renovated or built with MTW funds, so true holds without a nine-unit threshold.

set.prevailing_wage_basis: 24 CFR 983.153(c) (current eCFR, as amended by the HOTMA rule): labor standards apply to PBV development activity; for development involving nine or more contract units (whether or not completed in stages), the owner and its contractors must pay Davis-Bacon wages and comply with CWHSSA and 29 CFR part 5. If the PHA lets development start before an Agreement or HAP contract (983.154(f) or 983.157(b)(2)), labor standards run from proposal submission or the PHA board resolution approving project-basing. 24 CFR 983.4 cross-references the same labor standards for development of nine or more assisted units. Statutory basis is 42 U.S.C. 1437j(a), which covers projects with nine or more units assisted under section 1437f where the agreement is made before construction or rehabilitation begins. Does not apply to PBV on existing housing or to developments with eight or fewer PBV units. https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-24/subtitle-B/chapter-IX/part-983 ; https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/42/1437j
set.audit_note: PW audit Nov 10, 2026: true confirmed for PBV new construction or rehab with nine or more contract units (24 CFR 983.153(c), 983.4, 42 U.S.C. 1437j(a)); not triggered for existing housing PBV.

reason: Current 24 CFR 983.153(c) and 983.4 confirm Davis-Bacon on PBV development of nine or more contract units, not on existing housing.

set.prevailing_wage_basis: 42 U.S.C. 1437j(a) (Section 12 of the 1937 Act): any contract for loans, contributions, sale or lease under the Act must require Davis-Bacon wages for laborers and mechanics employed in development of the project, so public housing development or mixed-finance public housing work is covered with no unit threshold; the same section covers projects with nine or more Section 8 assisted units under an agreement made before construction or rehabilitation. Where repositioned units convert to PBV and are newly built or rehabilitated, 24 CFR 983.153(c) applies Davis-Bacon at nine or more contract units (also 983.4); PBV on existing housing is not covered. RAD conversion labor rules follow the RAD notice, which was not opened here. Labor Code 1720(c)(1) also removes the private residential exemption for projects built under an agreement with a local public housing authority. https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/42/1437j ; https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-24/subtitle-B/chapter-IX/part-983
set.audit_note: PW audit Nov 10, 2026: true kept; basis restated from the statute text and current 24 CFR 983.153(c) and 983.4 (public housing development has no unit floor; PBV conversions need nine or more contract units with development). RAD Davis-Bacon notice not opened (HUD URL returned 404).

reason: Statute and current PBV rule confirm Davis-Bacon on public housing development and on PBV development of nine or more contract units.
